desc:
An inversion of a permutation p of 1..n is a pair i < j with p[i] > p[j]. Return how many permutations of 1..n have exactly k inversions, modulo 1,000,000,007.

n = 3, k = 0  -> 1   [1,2,3]
n = 3, k = 1  -> 2   [1,3,2] [2,1,3]
n = 4, k = 2  -> 5
n = 2, k = 5  -> 0
hints: You cannot list permutations. Build them by inserting values one at a time and track the inversion count. What happens to the count when the new, largest value is inserted somewhere?

Take a permutation of 1..i-1 and insert the value i. If it is placed with t elements after it, it forms exactly t new inversions, and t can be anything from 0 to i-1. So dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j] + dp[i-1][j-1] + ... + dp[i-1][j-(i-1)].

That inner sum is a sliding window over the previous row, so keep a running prefix sum: dp[i][j] = dp[i][j-1] + dp[i-1][j] - dp[i-1][j-i] (drop the last term when j < i). Reduce modulo 1,000,000,007 and keep only two rows.
editorial: Let dp[i][j] be the number of permutations of 1..i with exactly j inversions. Insert the largest value i into a permutation of 1..i-1: the number of elements placed to its right, t, is between 0 and i - 1, each choice gives a different permutation, and creates exactly t new inversions because i is bigger than everything. Therefore dp[i][j] = sum_{t=0}^{min(j, i-1)} dp[i-1][j-t].

Computing that sum for each cell costs O(n) and leads to O(n2k). But consecutive cells share all but two terms, so with dp[i][j] = dp[i][j-1] + dp[i-1][j] - dp[i-1][j-i] (the last term only when j ≥ i) every cell costs O(1). Take care that subtraction modulo p must be adjusted to be non-negative.
Total O(n * k) time and O(k) space with two rolling rows. The answer is dp[n][k]; for k > n(n-1)/2 it is naturally 0.
solution:
def countPermutationsWithInversions(n, k):
    M = 1000000007
    prev = [0] * (k + 1)
    prev[0] = 1
    for i in range(2, n + 1):
        cur = [0] * (k + 1)
        cur[0] = 1
        for j in range(1, k + 1):
            v = cur[j - 1] + prev[j]
            if j >= i:
                v -= prev[j - i]
            cur[j] = v % M
        prev = cur
    return prev[k]
